1. identical inputs reproduce resample 0 exactly

tests.test: 2. identical inputs reproduce the WHOLE result
tests.implication: two runs of the same committed inputs print different intervals

tests.test: 3. REVERSED input order reproduces every resample
tests.implication: canonical sorting is missing or ineffective, so the caller's listing order selects different documents -- the defect withdrawn A29 measured

tests.test: 4. several permuted input orders give the IDENTICAL interval
tests.implication: the reported interval depends on how the caller happened to list its documents

tests.test: 5. a different event pattern CHANGES the interval, so the statistic is live
tests.implication: the interval is constant across event patterns, so it measures nothing and every reproducibility control above would pass on a dead quantity

tests.test: 6. changing the statistic identity CHANGES the draws, so domain separation is live
tests.implication: two different statistics share a draw sequence, so the population component of the identity is decorative and a P-robust variant could silently reuse P-head's draws

tests.test: 7. NEGATIVE -- a duplicate document identity REFUSES
tests.implication: a repeated document is silently weighted twice, though the document is the independent unit (8.3, red-team #7)

tests.test: 8. NEGATIVE -- an empty document set REFUSES
tests.implication: N = 0 produces a division by zero or a vacuous interval instead of refusing

tests.test: 9. NEGATIVE -- a non-boolean event REFUSES
tests.implication: a bare 0/1 is accepted -- it would work silently in sum() because bool subclasses int, so the wrong type would never be seen
